blindSpots: Killed-in-flight agent prefixes. Every heuristic looks at PROMPTS; the actual loss is an Agent whose result never came back. Measure it structurally: join each Agent tool_use id to its tool_result in the parent transcript; any agent jsonl with no matching result is 100% dead spend, priced by max-per-message output + cache tokens. On the one confirmed episode this gives 32,729 output / ~1.57M ctx over 26 requests exactly, with no window-guessing, and it also catches Ctrl-C, TaskStop, crashes and orphaned background agents, not just limit blocks.

Fanout redundancy measured on OUTPUTS rather than prompts. Jaccard over Agent prompts is the wrong instrument in both directions: deliberately-different lenses in one fanout score low while being highly redundant, and here two runs of the literally identical lens scored only 0.46-0.55. Measure: normalize each agent's returned findings (file+line+claim), dedupe across the fanout, and report unique-finding yield per agent and marginal yield of the Nth agent. MEMORY already records that one adversarial round beat 8 parallel lenses - that is a yield curve nobody has ever plotted.

Work that completed correctly and was never used. No prompt shape at all. Measure: for each subagent result or written artifact, check whether any later assistant turn quotes it, any commit touches it, or any PR body cites it within N turns; flag expensive unreferenced outputs. This is what killed the '33 findings from the dead verify lanes' and would price reports written for nobody.

Instruments that can never pass - the repo's own #1 rule, and the source of all three 2026-08-12 incidents. Measure from git, not transcripts: for every commit that introduces a gate/check/probe, look for a PASS on a known-good input before its first reported FAIL; flag any check whose entire history is FAIL. Transcript-side tell: a failing assertion resolved by editing the assertion rather than the system.

Silent-zero results built on (urllib '0 hits', grep blind to UTF-8, would_write=0). Measure: flag any tool result that is empty/zero-count and is then cited in a conclusion without a positive control, using a per-command-class baseline (this grep shape returns N elsewhere, 0 here). Charge everything downstream of the false zero.

Self-caught dead ends. The correction heuristic needs an OPERATOR correction; when the assistant catches itself there is no prompt to key on. Measure: detect assistant self-negation ('has been a no-op all along', 'that was wrong', 'I caused that') and charge the span back to the first tool call on that approach. This is the only way to see the ~5-minute CDP 'real input events' detour or the smoke-dist rename churn.

Cross-session rework. All six heuristics are intra-session or identical-prompt, so a defect shipped by session A and paid for by session B is invisible. Measure: link fix/revert commits and workJournal 'supersedes' forward-pointers back to the introducing commit, and charge session B's tokens to session A's skipped verification.

Rediscovery of things already written down. Measure: similarity of a session's stated conclusions against MEMORY.md / docs/workJournal.md, conditioned on whether the session actually read that file first; a high-similarity conclusion reached without the read is re-derivation.

Polling and waiting spend: repeated `gh run watch` / status calls on one resource id, including one window that watched the same run backgrounded and then foregrounded. Measure: repeated identical commands against the same resource id, and the tokens between first and last poll.

The census itself has no positive control. 10 of 11 nominations were refuted and the survivor was right for a different reason, which by the repo's own rule makes the instrument the suspect. Measure: seed a known waste episode (e.g. this confirmed one, or any unreturned-agent window) and require the detector to flag it before any FAIL it produces is reported.
